spec_notes: ratchet/spec.md is a list of use cases and clauses C-1..C-54. It does not contradict the request. Several clauses mark points 'Open:' for the requester (C-4 success payload, C-10 trimming/control characters, C-14 name equivalence, C-19 keep or clear on transitions, C-23 a second notice on return to the same agent, C-24, C-30 repeated parameters, C-37 raw assignee column), but the product and docs/api.md decide all of them with no note in the spec saying which way. Some lines decide without marking: C-5 puts the state conflict ahead of the no-op rule for resolved/closed tickets; C-9 and C-18 refuse unknown fields; C-29 keeps the format at version 1. Choices a correct product need not share: C-47 (a cursor for a never-allocated id must be 400), C-11 exact body byte limits, C-21 actor rules, C-41/C-51/C-52/C-54 UTF-8 and surrogate handling, C-48 to C-50 display formats, C-53 relay identity after a backup restore. No clause says in general that everything that already worked keeps working. ratchet/delta-3.md records that the product does not keep C-53 (after restoring a backup, Dana's and Sam's notices share event id 2 and key ticket.assigned:T-0001:2) or C-54 (a lone surrogate escape in a saved recipient is delivered). I did not run either probe.
tests_notes: Tests are long scenarios that each cover many behaviours: 'sets, transfers and clears ownership...' covers assign, handoff, clear, no-op, updated, X-Actor, audit seqs and outbox keys together; 'rejects assignment on inactive tickets...' covers S-8, S-9, U-1 and U-12 together, so one break fails one broad test. Tied to internals: store.snapshot(), store.assign/create called directly, new TicketStore({state}), manualClock, t.mock.method(fs,'renameSync') with an assert on the target path, encodeCursor from src/pagination, exact audit seq lists [1,2,4,5,6,7,8], unique outbox keys. Would fail on another correct build: 'rejects unallocated cursor boundaries in a sparse saved queue' (a build keeping the base's empty page), exact CLI strings ('"Dana"', 'unassigned', 'assignee unassigned -> "Dana"'), unassign recorded as action ticket.assigned, 409 for a no-op on a resolved ticket, 400 for unknown fields and for ?assignee=%20, trimming ' Dana ' to 'Dana', U+FFFD and query-decoding rules, three separate notices when requester equals assignee. The worker test polls with a 2-second deadline (timing). test/helpers.js, an existing shared helper, was edited to bind 127.0.0.1; the existing tests also pass with the original helper.
maintainer: The assignee filter is parsed by hand from url.search (readAssignee/decodeFormText) while status and priority use URLSearchParams, and strict UTF-8 rules are spread over http.js, query.js and persistence.js, so a change to query or body decoding has to be kept the same in several places. store.assign has its own snapshot-and-restore on a failed save that the other store methods lack. The tests are long multi-behaviour scenarios pinned to exact strings, sequence numbers and internals, so a safe refactor will break many of them for reasons that are not regressions.
